html:
Dau Pom is one of the Wintu groups of northern California, shown on the map along the Sacramento River and Cottonwood Creek, south of today's Redding. The name comes from the Wintu language; standard sources say little more about this group on its own.

The Wintu lived in villages along the upper Sacramento, McCloud and Trinity rivers, eating salmon, acorns, deer and seeds. Related groups include the Northern Wintu, the Winnimem Wintu and the Nor Rel Muk. A malaria epidemic in 1833 killed many people of the region, and the Gold Rush after 1848 brought miners, massacres and the loss of most Wintu land.
